CveFindings.Name: Apache Log4net: Silent log event loss in XmlLayout and XmlLayoutSchemaLog4J due to unescaped XML 1.0 forbidden characters
CveFindings.Description:
[CVE-2026-40021](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4f7c-pmjv-c25w): Apache Log4net XML layouts can silently drop log events when processing unescaped XML 1.0 forbidden characters.

Severity: MEDIUM

Affected dependencies:
- log4net 2.0.10 (affected range < 3.3.0), declared in eShopPorted/eShopPorted.csproj and src/eShopLegacyMVC/eShopLegacyMVC.csproj

Recommended fix:
- Upgrade log4net to 3.3.0 or later.

CveFindings.Name: Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions in Newtonsoft.Json
CveFindings.Description:
[CVE-2024-21907](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5crp-9r3c-p9vr): Newtonsoft.Json is vulnerable to improper handling of exceptional conditions.

Severity: HIGH

Affected dependencies:
- Newtonsoft.Json 12.0.1 (affected range < 13.0.1), declared in src/eShopLegacyMVC/eShopLegacyMVC.csproj

Recommended fix:
- Upgrade Newtonsoft.Json to 13.0.1 or later. The ported project declares 13.0.2, which is outside the affected range.

CweFindings.Name: Use of Obsolete Function
CweFindings.Description: The code uses deprecated or obsolete functions, which suggests that the code has not been actively reviewed or maintained.
CweFindings.Explanation: Serializing.SerializeBinary and DeserializeBinary instantiate System.Runtime.Serialization.Formatters.Binary.BinaryFormatter (Serializing.cs:11,19). BinaryFormatter is obsolete in modern .NET and remains a legacy serialization API.

CweFindings.Name: Incorrect Conversion between Numeric Types
CweFindings.Description: When converting from one data type to another, such as long to integer, data can be omitted or translated in a way that produces unexpected values. If the resulting values are used in a sensitive context, then dangerous behaviors may occur.
CweFindings.Explanation: The legacy sequence generator converts the SQL sequence result from Int64 to int (CatalogItemHiLoGenerator.cs:23; CatalogDBInitializer.cs:328-329), while catalog_hilo is explicitly defined as a bigint sequence (dbo.catalog_hilo.Sequence.sql:4-9). Values outside the int range overflow when used as catalog identifiers.

CweFindings.Name: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value
CweFindings.Description: The product allocates memory based on an untrusted, large size value, but it does not ensure that the size is within expected limits, allowing arbitrary amounts of memory to be allocated.
CweFindings.Explanation: CatalogController.Index accepts pageSize as an unbounded query parameter (CatalogController.cs:22) and CatalogService.GetCatalogItemsPaginated applies Take(pageSize) then materializes results with ToList (CatalogService.cs:25-31). A very large requested page can cause excessive result materialization and memory use.

CweFindings.Name: Use of Singleton Pattern Without Synchronization in a Multithreaded Context
CweFindings.Description: The product uses the singleton pattern when creating a resource within a multithreaded environment.
CweFindings.Explanation: When UseMockData is enabled, ApplicationModule registers CatalogServiceMock as a SingleInstance (ApplicationModule.cs:18-22). The singleton stores catalogItems in a mutable List and reads, modifies, and removes entries without synchronization (CatalogServiceMock.cs:12,33-67); concurrent requests can race while accessing shared catalog state.

CweFindings.Name: Unsynchronized Access to Shared Data in a Multithreaded Context
CweFindings.Description: The product does not properly synchronize shared data, such as static variables across threads, which can lead to undefined behavior and unpredictable data changes.
CweFindings.Explanation: When UseMockData is enabled, ApplicationModule registers CatalogServiceMock as a SingleInstance (ApplicationModule.cs:18-22). The singleton stores catalogItems in a mutable List and reads, modifies, and removes entries without synchronization (CatalogServiceMock.cs:12,33-67); concurrent requests can race while accessing shared catalog state.

CweFindings.Name: Improper Synchronization
CweFindings.Description: The product utilizes multiple threads or processes to allow temporary access to a shared resource that can only be exclusive to one process at a time, but it does not properly synchronize these actions, which might cause simultaneous accesses of this resource by multiple threads or processes.
CweFindings.Explanation: When UseMockData is enabled, ApplicationModule registers CatalogServiceMock as a SingleInstance (ApplicationModule.cs:18-22). The singleton stores catalogItems in a mutable List and reads, modifies, and removes entries without synchronization (CatalogServiceMock.cs:12,33-67); concurrent requests can race while accessing shared catalog state.

CweFindings.Name: Missing Synchronization
CweFindings.Description: The product utilizes a shared resource in a concurrent manner but does not attempt to synchronize access to the resource.
CweFindings.Explanation: When UseMockData is enabled, ApplicationModule registers CatalogServiceMock as a SingleInstance (ApplicationModule.cs:18-22). The singleton stores catalogItems in a mutable List and reads, modifies, and removes entries without synchronization (CatalogServiceMock.cs:12,33-67); concurrent requests can race while accessing shared catalog state.

CweFindings.Name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
CweFindings.Description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that is intended to identify a file or directory that is located underneath a restricted parent directory, but the product does not properly neutralize special elements within the pathname that can cause the pathname to resolve to a location that is outside of the restricted directory.
CweFindings.Explanation: PicController.Index combines the Pics directory with CatalogItem.PictureFileName (PicController.cs:38-40) without verifying the resolved path stays under Pics. CatalogController.Create/Edit bind PictureFileName from form input (CatalogController.cs:62,100), allowing a stored value containing traversal segments to be used in the file path.

CweFindings.Name: Relative Path Traversal
CweFindings.Description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize sequences such as .. that can resolve to a location that is outside of that directory.
CweFindings.Explanation: PicController.Index combines the Pics directory with CatalogItem.PictureFileName without canonicalizing or validating the result (PicController.cs:38-40). The picture filename can be supplied through catalog item create/edit form binding (CatalogController.cs:62,100), so relative traversal segments can escape the intended directory.

CweFindings.Name: Absolute Path Traversal
CweFindings.Description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize absolute path sequences such as /abs/path that can resolve to a location that is outside of that directory.
CweFindings.Explanation: PicController.Index uses Path.Combine(webRoot, item.PictureFileName) (PicController.cs:38-40) without checking whether the supplied filename is rooted; catalog forms bind PictureFileName from request data (CatalogController.cs:62,100). An absolute path can therefore bypass the Pics directory.

CweFindings.Name: Improper Control of Resource Identifiers ('Resource Injection')
CweFindings.Description: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not restrict or incorrectly restricts the input before it is used as an identifier for a resource that may be outside the intended sphere of control.
CweFindings.Explanation: PicController.Index uses CatalogItem.PictureFileName to select a filesystem resource through Path.Combine and File.ReadAllBytes (PicController.cs:38-45). The value is bound from catalog create/edit request data (CatalogController.cs:62,100), so external data controls which file resource is read.
